releaseNotes:
Full text by XQuery and XPath Full Text 3.0, with no Lucene dependency; directory collections; two security updates for hosts that use a `ResourcePolicy` or a large thread stack. Requires PhoenixmlDb.Core 2.6.1. W3C QT3: 31,294 of 31,325 (31 failing, the same cases as 3.1.0). W3C Full Text (XQFTTS 1.0.4): 672 of the 672 applicable cases (3.1.0: 271 of 685). ### Security: a file that changes between the policy check and the read (GHSA-v27x-ffg3-3wqq) Only hosts that use a `ResourcePolicy`, and whose allowed roots untrusted parties can write to, are affected. The library opens a file first, and the policy then judges the path of the file that is open, as the operating system reports it. A symbolic link put in place of the file, or of a directory on its path, after the check is not followed. This applies to `fn:unparsed-text`, `fn:json-doc`, `fn:doc`, `fn:doc-available`, `fn:collection`, module imports, schema and DTD loads, `xi:include` and `output:parameter-document`. Content that the host's resource resolver supplies, and locations that the host maps, do not change. See [GHSA-v27x-ffg3-3wqq](https://github.com/phoenixmldb/phoenixmldb-xquery/security/advisories/GHSA-v27x-ffg3-3wqq). ### Security: an error deep in recursion on a large thread stack (GHSA-rq84-6mj7-vqww) Only hosts that run queries on a thread with a large stack and set no step or depth limit are affected. A query that fails deep in recursion returns its error in time linear in the depth. The error code and message do not change. A query error or a cancellation does not carry a stack trace that spans every level. See [GHSA-rq84-6mj7-vqww](https://github.com/phoenixmldb/phoenixmldb-xquery/security/advisories/GHSA-rq84-6mj7-vqww). ### Breaking — read this when you upgrade - **`contains text` uses the defaults of Full Text 3.0** (Appendix C, #384): - No stemming: `"running" contains text "run"` is false. Write `using stemming`, or `declare ft-option using stemming;` for a module. - No stop words, and stop words apply to the query only (§3.4.7): a stop word in the query matches any one token. `"the walrus and the carpenter" contains text "the"` is true. - Diacritics insensitive: `"café" contains text "cafe"` is true. - `window N words` matches only words that are inside N words of each other. - Tokens do not cross element tags, except where a letter or digit touches the tag on both sides (`prototypes`). A paragraph ends at an element tag. A sentence ends at `.`, `!`, `?` and at the end of a paragraph. - **The public full-text syntax tree types change shape** (#384). Code that walks the syntax tree must change: - `FtMildNotNode.Include` and `Exclude` become `Operands`. - `FtSelectionWithFilters` is removed. The new node types are `FtWithOptionsNode`, `FtPositionFilterNode` and `FtExtensionSelectionNode`. - `FtMatchOptions` has option groups. - `FtContainsExpression.MatchOptions` becomes options on each primary plus `DefaultOptions`. `FtContainsExpression.Ignore` holds the `without content` expression. - `FtContainsOperator.WordOperators` becomes `EmbeddedOperators`, and the operator has `Ignore`. - A walker must visit the embedded expressions: weight, times range, window size, distance range and ignore. `FtSelectionNode.AllExpressions()` lists them all. `FullTextEngine.Analyze`, `ContainsText`, `WithinWindow` and `FullTextAnalysisOptions` keep their signatures. - **`fn:serialize` with no parameters, or with a map that names no method, uses the xml method** (F&O 3.1, #387), as Saxon does. `serialize((true(), "a"))` gives `true a` (3.1.0: `true() "a"`). `serialize(map{...})` with no method gives SENR0001. - **A relative URI with no base URI gives an error** (#374). A query compiled from a string with no base URI does not read from the process working directory: `doc()` gives FODC0002, `json-doc()` gives FOUT1170 (as `unparsed-text()` does in 3.1.0), and `doc-available()` returns false. This applies with and without a `ResourcePolicy`. A relative `declare base-uri` with no base stays as written. A document that the host loaded into the store under a relative name, host-supplied content and mapped locations do not change. To read a local file, set `CompilationOptions.BaseUri` or give an absolute URI. The `xquery` CLI sets the base URI. - **`QueryEngine.Compile` has overloads that take a `CancellationToken`** (#371). The token is checked during parsing, each analysis and rewrite pass (imported modules too) and planning. A cancel gives `OperationCanceledException`. `ExecuteAsync(XQueryExpression, ...)` and `XQueryFacade` pass their token to the compile. The overloads without a token stay. A caller that has a token in scope and does not pass it gets analyzer warning CA2016, which stops a build with warnings as errors. - **`FullTextEngine.Analyze` has a second overload** (#381). A `` is ambiguous (CS0419). Name the signature in the reference. ### New: full text without Lucene (#381) `PhoenixmlDb.XQuery` depends on `Antlr4.Runtime.Standard` and `PhoenixmlDb.Core` only. The built-in analyzer gives the same tokens as the Lucene 4.8 chain of 3.1.0: the term, position and offsets of each token are equal on 15,051 files and on 2,000,000 random strings, under 7 option sets. A full-text index made with 3.1.0 stays valid. A host that uses Lucene itself references `Lucene.Net` directly and chooses its version. - `IFullTextAnalyzer`, `FtToken`, `FtAnalysisRequest`, `FullTextAnalyzerRegistry` and `StandardFullTextAnalyzer` (namespace `PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.FullText`) let a host register an analyzer for a language. `QueryEngine.FullTextAnalyzers` gives the registry to `contains text`, `phx:tokenize` and `phx:stem`. `FullTextEngine.Analyze(text, options, registry)` lets an index use the same registry. - The word boundaries follow UAX #29 over Unicode 6.3 data. The stemmer is Porter (1980). ### New: XQuery and XPath Full Text 3.0 (#384, #388) All of the Full Text 3.0 grammar: - match options on each primary: `("dog" using stemming) ftand "cat"`; - `weight {expr}`; - `occurs exactly|at least|at most|from … to … times`; - the positional filters `ordered`, `window`, `distance`, `same|different sentence|paragraph`, `at start`, `at end` and `entire content`, in any combination; - `without content `; - `using lowercase` and `using uppercase`; - `using stop words default`, `at "uri"` and `("a", …)`, with `union` and `except`; - `using thesaurus at "uri" relationship "…" N levels`, `thesaurus default` and `thesaurus ( … )`; - `using option prefix:name "value"`; - extension selections `(# pragma #) { … }`; - `declare ft-option using …;`; - `for $x score $s in …` and `let score $s := …`. The errors that the specification names: FTST0008, FTST0009, FTST0013, FTST0018, FTST0019, FTDY0016, FTDY0017, FTDY0020, XQST0089, plus XPST0003, XPTY0004 and XPST0081 where they apply. **Stop word lists and thesauri by URI** (#388). `IFullTextResourceResolver` (`QueryEngine.FullTextResources`) supplies the resource for `using stop words at "uri"` and `using thesaurus at "uri"`. `FullTextResources` is an in-memory resolver. `FullTextThesaurus` loads the W3C test format and its own format. With no resolver, a stop word URI gives FTST0008 and a thesaurus URI gives FTST0018. `using stop words default` uses the resolver's default list, else the built-in English list. ### New: index support for full text - **`FullTextAnalysisOptions.FoldDiacritics`** (#385) removes diacritics from the tokens of an index, so that the index finds the candidates of a diacritics-insensitive query. The default tokens do not change. - **A candidate-source hook for `contains text`** (#389): `IFullTextCandidateSource`, `IFullTextCandidateFilter`, `FtCandidateQuery` and `QueryEngine.FullTextCandidates`. With a source, `contains text` skips only the items that the source rules out, and the results do not change. With no source, the evaluation does not change. An index that answers the hook must give at least the candidates that the evaluator matches. ### New: directory collections (#390) `collection()` and `uri-collection()` read a local directory: `file:///data/?select=*.json;recurse=yes`. The parameters are those of Saxon: `select` (a glob), `match` (a regular expression), `recurse=yes|no`, `on-error=fail|warning|ignore` and `content-type`, separated by `;` or `&`. - `collection()` gives an `.xml` file as a document, a `.json` file as a map or array (as `json-doc()`), a text file as a string and any other file as `xs:base64Binary`. `uri-collection()` gives the URIs and reads no file. The order is the path order. - `ServerDefault` and a `ResourcePolicy` that denies files refuse the directory, and the directory is not listed. A resolver with `SuppliesAllContent` gives no listing. A listing does not leave the directory through `..` or a symbolic link, and a linked directory is not entered. Each file is authorised and read with the limits of `doc()`, `json-doc()` and `unparsed-text()`. `on-error` does not hide a refusal or a limit. - A relative directory URI with no base URI gives FODC0002. - Only the built-in `XdmDocumentStore` lists a directory. A host with its own `IDocumentResolver` keeps its own collection behaviour. - Differences from Saxon-HE 12.10: `on-error` also applies to a JSON parse error, and the order is the path order. - `doc()` keeps the cause of a retrieval error in its message. ### Serialization - **Indented XML output has the layout of Saxon** (#392, #393). With `indent=yes` and the xml method, an empty element is `` (3.1.0 in the `xquery` CLI: ``), and an element serialized with its XML declaration starts on the line after the declaration. Text directly after the declaration gets no line break. The xhtml and html methods keep `
`. A test that compares indented output byte for byte must update its expected files. - **`serialize()` keeps `" />"` in text, comments, processing instructions and CDATA sections** (#393). Only the end of an empty element changes. Through `XQueryFacade`, the xhtml method gives `
`. - **The XML declaration names the encoding that the caller gives, or `UTF-8`** (#393), on every path. 3.1.0 writes `utf-8` for a document node and in the CLI. - **A space between adjacent atomic values** with the xml, html and xhtml methods (#383). ### Also in this release - `fn:analyze-string` returns its result element with no parent (#386), so a path such as `analyze-string($s, $re)/*` works. - `generate-id()` comes from the identity of the node (#376). Two different nodes do not get the same id. The form of an id changes. - UCA collations apply `alternate=shifted` and the numeric strengths `1` to `5` (UTS #10, #379). - `fn:index-of#2` uses the default collation (#375). ### `xquery` CLI (ships on `cli-v3.2.0`) - Runs on **PhoenixmlDb.XQuery 3.2.0** and **PhoenixmlDb.Xslt 3.2.0**, so it includes the changes above and `fn:transform` from a query gets the 3.2.0 XSLT engine. Includes the fixes for GHSA-v27x-ffg3-3wqq and GHSA-rq84-6mj7-vqww. - **JSON sources** (#391): a `.json` source is its map or array, and it is the context item when it is the first source. A directory source also loads its `*.json` files: `collection()` gives the documents, then the JSON items. Input on stdin that starts with `{` or `[` is read as JSON. - **A source that cannot be loaded is an error** (#391): `Error: Cannot load source '': ` on one line, exit code 1. A stack trace only with `--verbose`. **Breaking:** 3.1.0 writes a warning for a missing source and then gives XPDY0002 with exit code 3. A script that tests for exit code 3 must change. - An empty element in indented output is `` (#392).
